summary: Lolo National Forest lookout site in Granite County, Montana; a July 1935 newspaper report of placement and tent-based staffing; listed as abandoned platform, not gone.

facts.design: lookout tower erected in trees, per a 1935 newspaper report
facts.status_note: firelookout.com and the Forest Fire Lookout Association both list the site as Abandoned; neither gives a year

staffing.status: manned, with lookouts living in tents

events.note: Missoulian item of July 12, 1935, as quoted by Forest Lookouts, reports the lookout placed; it is a placement report, not a build date
Report says both new lookouts were manned, with lookouts occupying tents

evidence.supports: new lookout placed at Cinnamon Bear in the Rock Creek district, July 1935
evidence.quote: Two new lookouts have been placed in the Rock creek district, one at Hogback, and the other at Cinnamon Bear.

evidence.supports: site manned, lookouts occupying tents, using towers erected in trees
evidence.quote: These have been manned, with the lookouts occupying tents, and using lookout towers erected in trees.

evidence.supports: item attributed to the Missoulian, as quoted by Forest Lookouts
Granite County, Montana, about 15 miles ENE of Stevensville
1930s camp about two miles from summit; marked abandoned
evidence.quote: 1930s: camp 2 miles ESE of summit 7231. Abandoned.

evidence.supports: Montana Lookouts list: Cinnamon Bear Point, Granite, Platform, Abandoned
evidence.quote: Cinnamon Bear Point Granite 46.55740 -113.76690 Platform Abandoned

corrections.why: firelookout.com and the Forest Fire Lookout Association both list this site as Abandoned. Neither says the structure was removed or destroyed, so Gone goes beyond the sources.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com gives only a 1930s camp, and the 1935 Missoulian item is the only dated report. The story treats 1935 as the date of placement, not of construction.

notes_for_editor: Status corrected from gone to abandoned: both sources say Abandoned, with no removal noted. No source gives a year for abandonment, so no abandoned event is recorded. The 1930s camp on firelookout.com and the 1935 placement report are both kept, and the 1935 date is a newspaper report quoted secondhand by Forest Lookouts; the Missoulian itself was not read. The summit figure 7231 on firelookout.com is unclear and is not used. Coordinates 46.5574, -113.7669 from the FFLA list match the record. No access or photo data found. Web searches used: 2.
